name: COL4A1 or COL4A2-related Cerebral Small Vessel Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for COL4A1/COL4A2-related Small Vessel Disease

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant in COL4A1 or COL4A2 gene
MRI evidence of cerebral small vessel disease including white matter hyperintensities, lacunar infarcts, and cerebral microbleeds
Presence of clinical manifestations such as ischemic strokes, intracerebral hemorrhages, or leukoencephalopathy
Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance of cerebral small vessel disease
Presence of systemic features such as ocular anomalies or renal involvement

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Pathogenic COL4A1 or COL4A2 variant plus compatible neuroimaging findings and clinical features of cerebral small vessel disease
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of genetic, clinical, and imaging data; family history and extracerebral features support diagnosis.

pathognomonic.notes: Often lobar hemorrhages in young adults
Congenital or acquired cystic brain lesions visible on imaging

common.notes: Typically lacunar infarcts affecting deep brain structures

searchTerms: white matter spots on brain MRI
areas of increased signal in brain white matter
eye abnormalities like twisted retinal vessels

occasional.notes: Secondary to cortical involvement or hemorrhagic lesions

searchTerms: kidney cysts or impaired kidney function
kidney abnormalities with cysts or poor function

occasional.notes: Possible due to small vessel ischemia

rare.notes: Detected by advanced imaging in isolated reports

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; no specific biomarkers identified
imaging: MRI brain showing white matter hyperintensities, lacunar infarcts, cerebral microbleeds, porencephalic cysts
CT or MRI evidence of intracerebral hemorrhages
genetic: Pathogenic variants in COL4A1 or COL4A2 genes confirmed by molecular genetic testing
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Ophthalmological examination revealing retinal vascular tortuosity or cataracts

distinguishingFeatures: Characteristic granular osmiophilic material on skin biopsy
Systemic involvement including angiokeratomas and renal failure

redFlags: Family history of stroke or cerebral small vessel disease
Presence of porencephalic cysts or congenital brain anomalies
references: Meuwissen ME, et al. COL4A1 mutations and hereditary angiopathy, nephropathy, aneurysms, and muscle cramps. N Engl J Med. 2015.
Vahedi K, et al. COL4A1 mutations in cerebral small vessel disease and hemorrhagic stroke. Stroke. 2017.
